meta.label: Client edition 007
meta.preheader: NIFTY 50 slipped 0.18% in the Muhurat session after seven straight gains; foreign investors bought ₹13,750 crore on Friday (provisional); markets are shut on Tuesday.
meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Mon 9 Nov: NIFTY 50 eases 0.18% in the Muhurat session; markets shut Tuesday

brief: In Sunday's special Muhurat session, which opened Samvat 2083, the NIFTY 50 slipped 0.18% to 24,986.40 and the Sensex 0.04% to 80,999.40, ending a seven-session run of gains (PTI, Upstox News).

Smaller companies did better: the NIFTY Smallcap 100 rose about 1% and advancing shares outnumbered decliners 3,127 to 917 (The Federal). Media and pharma indices led, with Sun Pharma up 3.17%, while bank, IT and realty indices fell (Analytics Insight).

Foreign investors bought a net ₹13,750 crore on Friday and ₹45,960 crore over the week of 2 to 6 Nov; domestic institutions sold (provisional, Upstox). The rupee closed Friday at 93.89 per dollar (PTI).
NSE and BSE are closed on Tuesday 10 Nov for Diwali Balipratipada. US consumer inflation for October is due on Tuesday and India's on Thursday.

outlook.headline: Oil, foreign flows and two inflation readings frame a holiday-shortened week

drivers.title: Crude oil
drivers.text: Brent fell more than 13% last week after the US midterm results, The National reported. Bloomberg put the drop above 16% as investors weighed the chance of US and Iran talks, and cited Rystad Energy's Jorge Leon saying US pressure does not mean a deal is close. India imports most of its crude, so oil prices reach the import bill, the rupee and fuel inflation.

drivers.title: Foreign flows
drivers.text: Foreign investors were net buyers of ₹45,960 crore in the cash market from 2 to 6 Nov while domestic institutions sold ₹24,197 crore (provisional, Upstox). Foreign flows feed into large-cap share prices and the rupee; provisional figures can be revised.

drivers.title: Inflation and the RBI
drivers.text: Eleven economists polled by Financial Express expect October retail inflation at 6.1%, against 5.54% in September; ICRA's Aditi Nayar also expects 6.1%. The RBI raised the repo rate to 5.50% in October (Business Standard). Inflation readings shape rate expectations, which reach bond yields and loan rates.

source.name: Financial Express poll via IPA Newspack

drivers.title: The rupee and bonds
drivers.text: The rupee firmed 52 paise on Friday on a softer dollar, lower crude and buoyant shares, PTI reported. The 10-year yield was 7.19% (Business Standard). Bond prices rise when yields fall.

global_cues.title: US yields and the Fed
global_cues.text: The US 10-year yield ended Friday near 4.86% after strong October payrolls. LSEG data put the chance of a quarter-point Fed rate rise on 9 Dec at 75%, Dow Jones reported. Higher US yields can weigh on foreign flows into Indian shares and bonds.

global_cues.title: The dollar
global_cues.text: The dollar index rose about 0.7% to 102.3 on Friday after the jobs data (JournalArta, Investrade). A firmer dollar tends to weigh on the rupee and other emerging-market currencies.

global_cues.title: Technology shares
global_cues.text: The Nasdaq rose 1.09% on Friday after Thursday's sell-off but ended the week lower. Moves in global technology shares reach Indian IT companies and foreign allocations.

events.title: Market holiday and US inflation
events.text: NSE and BSE are closed for Diwali Balipratipada. US October consumer prices are due; Bloomberg's survey median expects a 0.3% monthly rise in headline prices and 0.2% in core prices (Business Standard).

events.title: India inflation
events.text: MoSPI releases October retail inflation. The Financial Express poll's range runs from 5.8% to 6.2%.

events.text: US October producer prices are due (Upstox News).

events.title: US Federal Reserve
events.text: Monex's Nick Rees said a December rise would be close to fully priced unless inflation or the 4 Dec jobs report surprised on the low side (Dow Jones).

global.headline: US shares were mixed on Friday after strong jobs data; Asian and European markets fell
global.note: On Friday the Kospi fell 6.02%, with a 20-minute trading halt, and Japan's Nikkei fell nearly 6% (Trading Economics). Trading Economics reported Japanese shares more than 2% higher early on Monday.

us.title: The session
us.text: US shares partly recovered on Friday from Thursday's AI-led sell-off: the Nasdaq and S&P 500 rose while the Dow slipped (Trading Economics). Chip makers led, with AMD up about 11%.

us.title: Jobs
us.text: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, against a consensus of 65,000, and unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2% (Investrade, TradingKey).

us.title: Rates
us.text: The 10-year Treasury yield rose as much as 6 basis points to 4.9% before settling near 4.86% (Trading Economics).

events.title: US midterms and Iran
events.text: Democrats won both houses of Congress (The National), and Trading Economics reported that Iran sent a proposal through Qatar. The channel to India: crude prices and the import bill.

events.title: Shipping in the Gulf
events.text: Tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz continued at a near-record pace, according to UKMTO data cited by Trading Economics. The channel to India: oil supply and freight costs.

events.title: Central bank gold buying
events.text: The World Gold Council reported 61 tonnes of central bank net gold buying in September, the most in any month of 2026, led by Poland and China. The channel to India: international prices set domestic gold rates.

commentary.text: Gold and silver fell on Friday after strong US payrolls as the dollar strengthened, Trading Economics reported; The National said markets weighed whether the Fed would keep rates high.
Trading Economics linked the week's gain in gold to safe-haven demand after the US midterm results and a move out of AI-linked shares.
The World Gold Council reported 61 tonnes of central bank net buying in September, led by Poland and China.

highlights.text: Small cap funds took the largest equity inflow in September at ₹9,039 crore, followed by mid cap funds at ₹7,835 crore and flexi cap funds at ₹6,702 crore; ELSS funds saw a net outflow of ₹662 crore.
ETFs took in ₹15,501 crore net: equity ETFs ₹9,960 crore, gold ETFs ₹4,451 crore and silver ETFs ₹1,974 crore.
Investors added 27.12 lakh folios in September, taking the total to 28.62 crore.

fund_news.text: Three of the fund house's international funds stopped taking new money from 4 Nov, including instalments on existing SIPs, Value Research reported.

nfo_summary.text: Five new fund offers on Cafemutual's 5 November list remain open on 9 November by their closing dates: a fixed maturity plan, an energy ETF, a silver ETF, a silver fund of funds and a realty index fund; three of them close on 9 November. Each scheme's category, riskometer level and terms are in its scheme information document. This list is reported for information only and is not a recommendation.

regulatory.text: From 1 April 2027, mutual fund schemes may net the cash they pay and receive for outright cash-market trades within a scheme; securities still settle trade by trade.

Since 1 November, direct plans are the default option on fund houses' own digital platforms; regular plans remain available, and investors who choose one there are told it carries a higher expense ratio.

category_explainer.text: Under SEBI's categorisation rules, a flexi cap fund must invest at least 65% of its assets in equity and equity-related instruments, with no minimum or maximum for large, mid or small cap companies. Because the manager can change the mix across company sizes, the scheme's risk can change with its holdings, and each scheme's riskometer level is set out in the fund house's own documents. These are equity schemes, so their value rises and falls with share prices.

learn.title: What Muhurat trading is
paragraphs: Muhurat trading is a short special session that NSE and BSE hold on Diwali to mark the start of the new Samvat year in the Hindu calendar.
This year's session ran for a little over an hour on the afternoon of Sunday 8 November, opening Samvat 2083 (PTI). Trades in it create settlement obligations, as on a normal day (Kotak Neo).
Because the session lasts about an hour, it reflects far less trading than a full day; index levels over longer periods give a fuller picture of the market.
